claims.claim: ITC reaches 28 crore Indian households and its new FMCG businesses have annual consumer spend above ₹37,000 crore.
claims.note: Reported by the company; useful for scale, but not independent evidence of customer loyalty or economic moat.

claims.claim: ITC's distribution network reaches nearly seven million outlets, more than 40% directly, and UNNATI serves over 800,000 outlets.
claims.note: Strong evidence of reach; outlet count alone does not prove exclusivity, throughput or pricing power.

claims.claim: ITC holds leading positions in branded atta, bridge snacks, cream biscuits and notebooks.
claims.source: ITC Report and Accounts 2026, p.75, citing NielsenIQ and Kantar
claims.note: Category-specific rankings are stronger than a generic FMCG leadership claim; full multi-year share history remains absent.

claims.claim: The sharp increase in cigarette taxation may strengthen illicit trade and disrupt legal-industry volumes.
claims.source: ITC Report and Accounts 2026, pp.69-73; ITC FY26 results statement
claims.note: The tax change is factual; the magnitude of legal-volume substitution is a forward-looking management assertion requiring FY27 evidence.

claims.claim: Recent digital-first and organic FMCG businesses have scaled to more than ₹1,350 crore annualised revenue.
claims.note: Revenue scale is not equivalent to profitability or adequate return on acquisition cost.
